newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. says still concerned over EU wheat subsidies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says still concerned over EU wheat subsidies.

text.p: The United States is still concerned about the European Union's use of subsidies to support its wheat exports, a U.S farm official said on Friday.
The United States feels that despite bumper crops in the main producing countries, historically low stocks do not warrant the use of EU subsidies to boost exports, the official said.

"We have been following with great concern ever since subsidies were reinstated in September. As we said back then and as we said since then we simply do not believe that export subsidies are warranted in the current market situation," Timothy J. Galvin told Reuters.
Galvin, associate administrator for the USDA's foreign agricultural service, was speaking at a farm conference organised by the AGRA magazine.
"It is true that some producers have had relatively good crops - the EU, Australia, Argentina - but nethertheless world stocks remain historically tight," he added.
He also said it was disappointing to see a major player choosing to subsidise exports at a time when competition among world suppliers was severe.

Galvin added that the United States had voiced its concern over EU subsidies on a regular basis with EU officials and more recently when U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman met with EU farm Commissioner Franz Fischler at a food summit in Rome.
EU oficials argue that export subsidies are needed to bridge the gap between European and world prices.
But to placate U.S. critics who want the U.S. to fight subsidies with subsidies, Brussels has repeatedly pleged not undercut U.S. wheat prices.
In recent weeks it has drawn a delicate balance between sticking to that pledge and maintaining a steady flow of exports.
Asked to comment on this policy, Galvin just said, "It still concerns us. The fact is they are subsidising and we are not. So anytime that is the case we are very concerned."
